item.description:
The two rings that offered the same apps now know about each other, and a pinned app can look like whatever you want it to.

Pins in the window ring

Quick access can hold the front of the window ring as well — of every page, not just the first. The direction to a pin is then the same on the third page as on the first, which is the entire point of pinning something.

A pinned app that happens to be running is taken out of the window list and given that app's windows, so the pin is the same slot the switcher would have shown, in a place that does not move, rather than a second slot for the same app. Its fan still opens.

Off by default. Pins spend slots that would otherwise show windows, and Settings states the trade with your own numbers rather than in the abstract: how many slots the pins take on each page and how many are left for windows.

Pins can carry their own icon

An SF Symbol, an emoji, or an image file. Leave it and you get the app's own icon, which is the right answer nearly always.

Image files are copied into the app's support folder rather than remembered by path. Remembering the path is the obvious thing, and the obvious thing turns a ring slot blank the first time you tidy your Downloads folder, for reasons nothing on screen can explain.

The shortcut rows gained image upload at the same time — they share the picker.

Fixed

  • Pinned slots read "Opera.app" if you have Finder set to show every extension, while the same app in the window ring read "Opera". The bundle's own name is used now, so the two agree.
  • The page dots miscounted once pins were at the front, because the page count was being worked out from how many slots were on screen.
  • --demo built its own slots and skipped the merge, which made the one way to look at this feature the one way that did not have it.

Requirements

macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon. MiddleRing needs Accessibility permission — that is what lets it read the window list and bring a window forward. Screen Recording is only requested if you turn live previews on.

Install

If you are on 0.3.0 or later this arrives on its own. Otherwise open the DMG, drag MiddleRing to Applications, launch it, and grant Accessibility when asked. It lives in the menu bar; there is no Dock icon.

Signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning.

The ring now says when letting go will close it, and the plates behind the icons are optional.

The centre says what it does

Releasing with the cursor in the middle has always cancelled. Nothing said so. The ring used its accent colour to mean "this is what you are about to pick" and had no way to say "this is what you are about to *not* pick", so the safest thing you could do looked exactly like doing nothing.

It turns red now — the hub, the pointer, and the label, which reads Kapat. Three channels rather than one: colour alone is not a message to anyone who does not see red as red.

Only after you have aimed at something at least once, or once the ring is parked. The ring opens with the cursor already in the middle, and a warning that fires every single time is one you learn to ignore.

Bare icons

Görünüm can take the material plate out from behind the icons. What is left is the icon and a shadow — depth without a panel — and the icon grows into the space the plate used to take up.

Selection survives it as a tight ring of accent light around the icon itself. Window previews keep their plate: the image is clipped to it, and a photograph with no edge bleeds into anything light behind it.

Settings that say what they do

Görünüm needed this most. Three sliders labelled with words that described the implementation rather than the effect, and nothing explaining any of them. They are grouped now, every control has a line saying what it changes, and "Ölü bölge" is "Merkez boşluğu".

Elsewhere: a modifier on a trackpad gesture now says that it is a requirement, not a bonus — left unsaid, the first thing it does is make the gesture look broken to whoever set it and forgot. The Screen Recording note links to the permission instead of reciting the path to it. The shortcut rows have column headings.

Updating

If you are on 0.3.0 this one arrives on its own — MiddleRing checks for itself now. 0.2.0 and earlier still need one manual install, after which they are on the same footing.

Signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning.

Two more rings, a third thing right-click can do, trackpad gestures that take modifiers — and, from this version on, MiddleRing updates itself.

Quick access ring

A fixed list of apps in the order you put them in. The switcher is ordered by recency, which is the right answer for switching and the wrong one for muscle memory; this ring never moves, so the direction is learnable.

A pinned app that is closed keeps its slot, shows a dimmed icon, and launches when you commit it. One that has been uninstalled leaves the ring rather than sitting there failing.

App shortcut ring

Keystrokes for whichever app is in front, under names you gave them. Open it in Figma and you get Figma's; open it in a browser and you get the browser's. Committing a slot posts that keystroke straight to the app.

A slot shows the keystroke by default — using the ring is how you stop needing it — or a symbol picked from a short grid of SF Symbols and emoji, which is quicker to pick out of a circle at speed. A "global" set sits under whatever the frontmost app contributes, so the ring is not empty in an app you have not got round to configuring.

Solo

Right-click a slot to minimize everything that does not belong to that app and switch to it. App-level even when you aimed at a single window: "leave me with this one" means the app you are about to work in.

A second solo on the same app restores exactly what the first one minimized — not everything currently minimized, which would also undo whatever you had tidied away yourself.

Trackpad gestures take modifiers

Kept separate from a ring's keyboard and mouse modifiers, so binding a ring to ⌃⌥⌘L does not silently demand ⌃⌥⌘ on its finger gesture too.

That also makes two fingers bindable. On its own it is the system's secondary click and taking that from every app is not a setting anyone would look for again; under ⌃ or ⌥ it is a gesture nothing else claims.

It updates itself now

The hard part of updating was never noticing that a new version exists — it is replacing a running app in place with its Developer ID signature intact, and getting that wrong costs you the Accessibility grant along with the app. So this uses Sparkle, and the update feed is signed with a key whose private half never leaves the developer's machine.

This is the last version you have to install by hand. 0.2.0 shipped without an updater, so it cannot pull this one down; from 0.3.0 onward MiddleRing checks for itself and offers the update in place. There is a "Check for updates" item in the menu bar and a switch in Settings › Genel if you would rather it did not.

Also

  • Rings are a list internally rather than two hand-copied blocks of settings, so the next one costs an enum case. Triggers you had already chosen are migrated; nothing needs re-binding.
  • Fixed: nested Sparkle components failed notarization on the first attempt, which is worth saying out loud because codesign --deep --strict passes on exactly that mistake.
